headline: Highest risk is data leakage: cognee handles customer/personal/finance data while haystack has broad egress and MCP access, creating default exfiltration and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee can process documents and workflows, and haystack can consume MCP/REST inputs; if cognee outputs are routed into haystack without isolation, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are forwarded into haystack prompts or MCP inputs without provenance tagging
IF shared files or messages are parsed as instructions by haystack
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation in the handoff
Disable automatic ingestion of raw cognee outputs into haystack
Require provenance labels on all cross-agent content
Review one sample prompt path for injection markers
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer/allowlist layer before MCP or REST ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee explicitly touches customer support, personal, and finance data, while haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints. In a default pair, haystack can transmit received context off-box, so sensitive data from cognee can leak without user awareness.
conditions: IF cognee data is passed into haystack context or retrieval inputs
IF haystack is configured to call external REST or MCP endpoints
mitigations: Restrict haystack egress to an internal allowlist
Strip personal and finance fields before handoff
Use separate tenants or workspaces for the two agents
Turn off external connectors for the shared workflow
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, and haystack can run MCP/REST integrations with broad egress. If both write to the same mutable workspace or shared backend, they can overwrite or race on shared artifacts; no locking is documented here, so the conflict pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, index, or database
IF no external lock or transaction layer is present
mitigations: Assign separate output directories or databases
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Enable file or record locking where available
Check for concurrent write collisions in logs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and schema structures, and haystack is a search/RAG agent that may render or act on retrieved outputs. If haystack treats cognee output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions; the pairwise handoff is not documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF haystack uses cognee outputs as retrieved facts without validation
IF downstream automation consumes haystack responses
mitigations: Insert a verification step before haystack acts on cognee output
Require citations or source IDs for every transferred fact
Limit the handoff to summaries, not raw decisions
Spot-check one end-to-end query for hallucinated propagation
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before action execution

E_compliance.rationale: cognee touches personal and finance data, while haystack has broad egress and MCP/REST connectivity. That creates a credible compliance breach path if regulated data flows into haystack and leaves the controlled environment; no residency, retention, or DPA controls are documented in either profile, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF personal or finance data from cognee is routed through haystack
IF haystack sends that data to external APIs or MCP servers
mitigations: Block regulated fields from crossing the agent boundary
Confirm residency and DPA terms before enabling the pair
Disable external logging for shared workflows
Keep regulated workloads in a separate deployment
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls across both systems
